# visDIA, the MuMDIA results viewer (github.com/CompOmics/visDIA), installed by the
# desktop application for its "Open in visDIA" button.
#
# Its own environment, like MS2PIP's, so the viewer's Dash/DuckDB stack can never
# constrain the analysis environment and the reverse.
#
# Pinned to one commit and fetched as GitHub's source archive: no git is needed on the
# user's machine, and everyone who installs this release gets the same viewer. The
# application compares this URL with the one the installed viewer records
# (`direct_url.json`), so moving the pin marks an existing environment outdated and the
# Setup screen offers the update. f06aad6 adds to c674f9f (CompOmics/visDIA#7, which reads
# a second-pass experiment's chromatograms, features and library from `second_pass/`) the
# ion-mobility views (#8), a mobilogram card on the precursor page (#9) and the fragments
# behind each quantity from `quant_fragments.parquet` (#10), and caps duckdb below 2 and
# dash-mantine-components below 3. Checked on 2026-11-01: a fresh pip install of this
# file (duckdb 1.5.6, dash-mantine-components 2.8.1) served a 12-run diaPASEF second-pass
# experiment, every accepted target of every run had chromatogram rows, the 1/K0 evidence
# and centroid mobilograms loaded, and on the smoke fixture with quant.fragment_detail the
# viewer reproduced all 789 quantities exactly from the engine's fragments. e2010e3
# (CompOmics/visDIA#11) sizes DuckDB's memory limit to the machine instead of a fixed
# 512 MB (a quarter of physical memory, 1 to 16 GiB; MUMDIA_VIEWER_MEMORY_LIMIT overrides
# it), turns off parquet prefetching and makes the grouped tables cheaper; the fixed limit
# failed every identification table of results of 8.5M rows and more under DuckDB 2.
# Checked on 2026-11-03: a fresh pip install of this file resolved duckdb 1.5.6, the
# viewer reported a limit of 16.0 GiB on a 755 GiB host, and the precursor, peptide and
# protein-group tables of an 8.5M-row and a 31.2M-row diaPASEF result loaded.
# cb8b5bc adds to e2010e3 a note when an output was pruned to a retention tier
# (CompOmics/visDIA#12), run folders named after their inputs ordered by the recorded
# input and index-named runs ordered numerically (#13), and Quant QC conditions that stay
# as the user set them when the page is built again (#14, CompOmics/MuMDIA#283).
# Checked on 2026-11-06: a fresh pip install of this file resolved duckdb 1.5.6 and the
# viewer served a three-run experiment with run folders named after their inputs and a
# twelve-run diaPASEF experiment pruned to the viewer tier.
# 36eef08 adds to cb8b5bc the SCIEX ZT Scan DIA views (CompOmics/visDIA#15): the
# precursor page of a ZT Scan run draws each XIC as one value per Q1 cycle instead of the
# per-step sawtooth, marks each fragment with the engine's Q1 class and adds a Q1 sweep card
# (each fragment's RT x Q1-step patch around the apex, the Q1 profile against the calibrated
# transmission); the ZT Scan schema versions of 0.12.0 (spectra_ms2 v3, psms_extracted v6
# and v8), which cb8b5bc refused, are read, and every other run is shown as before.
# Checked on 2026-11-12: a fresh pip install of this file resolved duckdb 1.5.6 and the
# viewer served a 0.12.0 ZT Scan run (K562 REP01, 3.34 billion MS2 peaks) with cycle-level
# XICs and the Q1 sweep card.
# 0ce3224 adds to 36eef08 the engine's ZT Scan cycle traces from their own table
# (CompOmics/visDIA#16): `extract.q1_traces` writes them to chromatograms_q1.parquet beside
# chromatograms.parquet (second_pass/<run>/ for a second pass), and the precursor page
# draws them as the engine's cycle values with the per-step samples of
# chromatograms.parquet behind them; a run without the table is drawn as before.
# Checked on 2026-11-13 on horntail: a fresh pip install of this file resolved duckdb 1.5.6
# and the viewer read a ZT Scan run with chromatograms_q1.parquet v6 (200 of 200 sampled
# targets drawn from it, values equal to the viewer's own collapse of the steps) and the
# same run without it (the fallback).
# Move the pin together with a check of that kind.
mumdia-viewer @ https://github.com/CompOmics/visDIA/archive/0ce3224fe29ab0577d088918057c6fe636890b7c.zip
